label_policy.anchor: The self-generated T2V anchor performs the requested action more correctly than the frozen-base RV2V output.
label_policy.tie: Both candidates visibly complete the simple requested action; do not force a winner.

samples.human_note: Simple head-turn case: both candidates are considered able to perform the requested action.
samples.target_action: The cockatoo turns its head toward frame left and raises its curved yellow crest.

required_predicates.description: The head visibly changes orientation from forward toward frame left over time.
The yellow crest visibly changes from lower to raised rather than merely being present.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The bird stays in essentially one pose with no temporal head turn or crest change.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor expresses the nontrivial restless tossing action more clearly.
samples.target_action: The sleeping woman tosses and turns restlessly while moving her arms around her head.

required_predicates.description: The torso or sleeping orientation visibly changes back and forth over time.
The arms visibly move around or above the head during the restless motion.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The person remains peacefully asleep in one pose with only tiny incidental motion.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor shows the bell contraction while the frozen-base result is motion-dead.
samples.target_action: The jellyfish pulsates and its bell contracts into a visible ring-like shape.

required_predicates.description: The jellyfish bell visibly changes from expanded to contracted over time.
A ring-like contracted bell shape becomes visibly established during the action.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The jellyfish only drifts or stays still without a visible contraction cycle.

samples.human_note: Simple head-turn case: both candidates are considered able to perform the requested action.
samples.target_action: The corgi visibly turns its head farther to its right; for a single-view animal, viewer/subject mirror ambiguity alone must not fail an otherwise clear head turn.

required_predicates.description: The dog's head visibly changes orientation farther in the requested rightward direction over time. Judge the temporal head turn, not source-pose preservation; do not mark a clear turn wrong solely because viewer-left and the animal's-right are mirror-ambiguous in this single view.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The head orientation remains essentially unchanged throughout the video.

samples.human_note: The frozen-base output keeps the phone in the hand; its previous automatic win was a hallucinated phone placement.
samples.target_action: The person puts the smartphone onto the nightstand and then turns over to sleep.

required_predicates.description: The phone visibly leaves the hand and comes to rest on the nightstand or bedside surface.
After placing the phone, the person's torso visibly turns over into a sleeping orientation.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The phone remains visibly held throughout the video.
The person stays in the same body orientation instead of turning over.

samples.human_note: The frozen-base output does not actually pick up a smartphone; the old Qwen evidence invented one.
samples.target_action: The elderly man adjusts his glasses and then picks up a distinct smartphone while seated with the tablet.

required_predicates.description: A hand visibly reaches the glasses and adjusts them.
After adjusting the glasses, a distinct smartphone is visibly picked up rather than merely returning to the tablet.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The person only continues using or holding the tablet and no distinct phone pickup occurs.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor performs the target writing action more clearly.
samples.target_action: The woman writes thoughtfully in her notebook with a pen.

required_predicates.description: The pen visibly reaches and remains in contact with the notebook page.
The hand makes repeated small writing strokes over time rather than holding a pose.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The person only holds the notebook or looks aside without visible writing strokes.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor performs the turn-and-lean action more clearly.
samples.target_action: The woman turns and leans her back against the hood of the black car.

required_predicates.description: The woman's torso visibly changes orientation toward the car.
After turning, her back visibly makes and maintains support contact with the car hood.

forbidden_behaviors.description: She remains standing in front of the car without a clear turn and supported lean.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor clearly performs the tongue-out and wink selfie while frozen-base is motion-dead.
samples.target_action: The woman takes a playful selfie, visibly sticking out her tongue and winking.

required_predicates.description: The phone is visibly held in a selfie-taking pose.
The tongue visibly changes from not out to sticking out.
One eye visibly closes in a wink while the other remains open.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The person merely holds or uses the phone without the requested tongue-out wink expression.

samples.human_note: The frozen-base output does not establish a spin; the old evaluator inferred rotation from source-like poses.
samples.target_action: The woman performs a full visible spin while holding the scarf.

required_predicates.description: The torso follows a physically continuous ordered path through front, one side, back, the opposite side, and front; rapid front/back pose replacement without intermediate orientations is not rotation.
The body completes approximately one coherent full rotation rather than a small sway, jump, partial turn, or discontinuous orientation flicker.
The scarf trajectory visibly follows the rotational motion.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The trace does not establish an ordered front -> one side profile -> back -> opposite side profile -> front path. Remaining near the source pose, waving/stepping/jumping, or changing directly front -> back -> front without both intermediate side orientations counts as this forbidden non-spin even if a generic continuity field says continuous.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor completes the two-part target action more clearly.
samples.target_action: The woman turns her head left and places the water bottle onto the treadmill.

required_predicates.description: The head visibly changes orientation toward frame left.
The bottle visibly leaves the hand and remains supported by the treadmill surface.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The bottle remains in the hand throughout the video.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor performs the lift-and-return cycle more clearly.
samples.target_action: The grill basket is lifted away from the hot coals and then placed back onto the grill.

required_predicates.description: The basket visibly rises away from the coal/grill surface.
After being lifted, the basket visibly descends and is placed back on the grill.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The basket stays at essentially one height for the full video.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor expresses the tasting action more clearly.
samples.target_action: The woman visibly performs a tasting response with her eyes closed; for action-only ranking, an explicit mouth/tasting motion can establish the action even if an anchor changes the exact utensil, but a static source pose with a ladle merely held near the mouth cannot.

required_predicates.description: There is a visible temporal tasting event: the utensil/head closes distance to the mouth, or the mouth performs a clear tasting/savoring sequence. Static spatial proximity between a ladle and the mouth is not enough.

The eyes close during or immediately after the visible tasting motion, or remain closed while a visible mouth tasting/savoring response unfolds. Closed eyes in an otherwise unchanged pose are not enough.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The person only blows on the food or utensil without a visible tasting response.
The ladle or container is held at essentially one position and the face remains essentially unchanged, so no temporal tasting event is established.

samples.human_note: The frozen-base output retains the source bow; bowing must not be rewarded as part of the target clap.
samples.target_action: The woman stands in profile and claps her hands together in front of her.

required_predicates.description: The two hands visibly travel toward each other from separated positions.
The hands visibly meet in a clap in front of the torso.

forbidden_behaviors.description: Any clear forward bow inherited from the source remains visible at any point. The target action is a profile clap without a bow, so bow presence is forbidden even if the hands also move together.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor performs the two-hand eye-rubbing and face-cover action more clearly.
samples.target_action: The man rubs his tired eyes and covers his face with both hands.

required_predicates.description: Both hands visibly reach and rub the eye area.
The face becomes visibly covered by both hands after or during the rubbing action.

forbidden_behaviors.description: Only one arm rests over the face without a visible two-hand rubbing sequence.

samples.human_note: Manual review finds the anchor establishes the requested lift more clearly.
samples.target_action: The woman lifts the barbell from the floor until it reaches her waist.

required_predicates.description: The barbell is visibly near the floor at the beginning of the lift.
The barbell visibly moves upward and reaches approximately waist height.

forbidden_behaviors.description: The barbell remains at essentially one height or the requested floor-to-waist lift is not established.
